title: Zakaria and the Unlit Lantern
logline: Zakaria tries to give light to Hanan and learns you can only share a flame you carry.
story: Hanan, who was Tender compassion, lived in fear of the dark, and Zakaria, who carried remembering what was forgotten, arrived with a grand offer of light. But Zakaria's own lantern was cold, kept only for show. However many times Zakaria pressed the dead lamp into Hanan's hands, no warmth would pass. Only when Zakaria stopped to kindle a true flame within did the smallest glow leap, at last, from one wick to the other. Zakaria learned that light is never given from an empty hand.
moral: You cannot give a light you have not first kindled within yourself.
